question: Which receptor on human cells does the COVID-19 virus (SARS-CoV-2) mainly attach to?
explanation: Great job! The virus uses its spike protein to lock onto ACE2 receptors, which are found in large numbers in our respiratory tract. You've got this!

question: What makes a 'cytokine storm' so dangerous in severe COVID-19 patients?

options.A: It causes widespread tissue damage and multi-organ failure
options.B: It permanently blocks the absorption of oral medications
options.C: It causes a sudden and permanent drop in blood pressure only
options.D: It immediately destroys all white blood cells in the body

explanation: Spot on! A cytokine storm is like an immune system overdrive. It floods the body with inflammatory signals that end up harming healthy organs. Keep up the good work!

question: How does COVID-19 mostly spread from person to person?

options.A: By drinking contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: Through the bite of infected mosquitoes and ticks
options.C: By consuming undercooked poultry and beef products
options.D: Through respiratory droplets from coughing and talking

explanation: You got it! Tiny droplets released into the air when people talk, cough, or sneeze are the main way the virus travels. Simple infection control basics!

question: Which mask is most important when doing a procedure that generates aerosols on a COVID-19 patient?

options.C: A simple clear plastic face shield alone
options.D: An N95 or higher respirator mask

explanation: That's correct! Procedures that create tiny floating mists require the tight seal and special filtration of an N95 respirator to keep you safe.

question: Which symptom is a very common clue that points specifically to COVID-19 over other flu-like viruses?

options.A: Sudden loss of taste or smell
options.D: Severe swelling of the salivary glands

explanation: Spot on! Losing your sense of taste or smell (anosmia and ageusia) is a classic hallmark sign of a SARS-CoV-2 infection. Easy to remember for your clinicals!

question: What room-air oxygen saturation level helps nurses classify a patient's COVID-19 illness as severe?
explanation: You nailed it! When a patient's oxygen level drops below 94% on room air, it means their lungs are struggling with gas exchange, pointing to severe illness.

question: What is the gold standard test used to confirm an active COVID-19 infection?

options.B: Basal metabolic panel and electrolyte screen
options.C: Complete blood count with differential analysis

explanation: Correct! The RT-PCR test picks up viral genetic material with high accuracy, making it the go-to test for catching an active infection.

question: Why is a high D-dimer blood result worrying in a COVID-19 patient?

options.A: It shows that the kidneys are failing to filter waste
options.B: It suggests an increased risk for abnormal blood clot formation
options.C: It proves the patient has a severe bacterial lung infection
options.D: It indicates permanent damage to the heart muscle valves

explanation: Well done! D-dimer is a protein left behind when clots break down. High levels mean the body is forming clots somewhere it shouldn't.

question: What do we mean by 'happy hypoxemia' in COVID-19 care?

options.A: Feeling overly energetic despite severe viral fatigue and muscle aches
options.B: Experiencing extreme chest pain while maintaining normal oxygen levels
options.C: Showing high fever and cough while blood pressure remains stable
options.D: Having dangerously low blood oxygen without feeling short of breath

explanation: You got it! Some patients have shockingly low oxygen levels yet feel completely fine, which is why checking vital signs with a pulse oximeter is so important.

question: A COVID-19 patient says they feel completely fine, but their pulse oximeter reads 88% on room air. What should you do first?

options.A: Wait for the patient to request oxygen before taking any action
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink more fluids and rest in bed
options.C: Discharge the patient home since they report feeling comfortable
options.D: Apply supplemental oxygen and notify the attending healthcare provider

explanation: Spot on! An 88% saturation is a red flag regardless of how good the patient feels. Always trust your machine and act fast to protect your patient.

question: Why do doctors prescribe the steroid dexamethasone to hospitalized COVID-19 patients?

options.A: To dissolve existing blood clots in the lower legs
options.B: To stimulate the appetite and prevent severe weight loss
options.C: To suppress severe and damaging body inflammation
options.D: To kill the coronavirus directly inside the lungs

explanation: Correct! Dexamethasone helps calm down that over-enthusiastic immune response that wreaks havoc on the lungs.

question: Why are blood thinners frequently given to patients admitted with moderate to severe COVID-19?

options.A: To lower elevated blood pressure readings during a fever spike
options.B: To prevent dangerous blood clots caused by inflammation and immobility
options.C: To thin the thick mucus secretions blocking the upper airways
options.D: To improve the ability of red blood cells to carry extra oxygen

explanation: You got it! COVID-19 makes the blood prone to clotting, so giving thinners helps stop dangerous conditions like DVT or pulmonary embolism.

question: What is the main benefit of placing a severe COVID-19 patient in the prone position (lying on their stomach)?

options.A: It improves oxygen exchange and lung expansion
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for intravenous lines
options.C: It prevents the patient from coughing during sleep
options.D: It allows the patient to feed themselves more easily

explanation: Well done! Gravity helps open up parts of the lungs that are pressed down when lying on the back, making it much easier for the patient to get oxygen.

question: When is ECMO (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation) usually considered for a COVID-19 patient?

options.A: Immediately upon admission before trying simple nasal cannula oxygen
options.B: As the first-line treatment for all patients with a mild cough
options.C: When the patient is ready to be weaned off all breathing support
options.D: When conventional mechanical ventilation fails to maintain adequate oxygen levels

explanation: Spot on! ECMO is a major rescue therapy saved for the toughest cases where regular ventilators just aren't doing the job anymore.

question: What do we call the ongoing health issues that linger for months after recovering from initial COVID-19?
explanation: Correct! 'Long COVID' is the term used when symptoms stick around long after the acute virus has cleared the body.

question: Which of these is a very common complaint from patients suffering from Long COVID?

options.C: Sudden bone fractures in the legs

explanation: You got it! Many people with Long COVID struggle with lingering tiredness and trouble concentrating, often called 'brain fog'.

question: What is the primary benefit of getting a COVID-19 vaccine?

options.A: Reducing the risk of severe illness and hospitalization
options.C: Guaranteeing that a person will never catch the virus
options.D: Eliminating the need for hand hygiene and masks

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines train your immune system to fight off the worst parts of the disease, keeping you out of the hospital.

question: What key advice should you give a patient with mild COVID-19 who is well enough to stay home?

options.A: Visit crowded public areas to build natural community immunity
options.B: Stop wearing a mask immediately once the fever drops
options.C: Avoid drinking fluids so that coughing spells decrease
options.D: Stay home in isolation to avoid spreading the virus to others

explanation: You nailed it! Self-isolating at home is the best way to protect your family members and community from catching the virus.
